newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Novartis in no hurry to buy.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Novartis in no hurry to buy.

text.p: Newly-formed Swiss life sciences giant Novartis AG said on Tuesday that it was in no hurry to make further acquisitions despite its strong balance sheet.

In an interview with Reuters, Novartis presdient Daniel Vasella said the group had strong cash flow of three billion Swiss francs a year while its net liquidity had risen sharply to 6.19 billion francs from 3.62 billion.

"This gives us the freedon strategically we need to act if we think something is attractive. But obviously it would be a mistake to feel pressured because you have money to rush in to an acquisition," said Vasella.

He said the group's "first emphasis" was on internal growth, but added that every area of Novartis's business would benefit from acquisitions, including Consumer Health, which is only seventh in its sector worldwide.
"The first duty Consumer Health has is to streamline the portfolio, focus on a few major brands and really promote and grow them to an adequate size," said Vasella.
Novartis said on Tuesday that it was in "advanced discussions with potential buyers" to sell 14 branded over-the-counter products in the U.S.

"The focus (at Consumer Healthcare) is first and above all on internal growth. Obviously we are keeping our eyes open (for acqisitions) but it would be a mistake to conclude that that is our first emphasis," said Vasella.
The president said he did not believe the recent wave of consolidation in the drugs industry, which included the formation of Novartis through the merger of Ciba and Sandoz, had run its course.
"I anticipate that there will be future transactions. When or who I can't tell but I don't believe consolidation is over," said Vasella.

However he said it was "still difficult to imagine" companies being able to achieve 10 percent shares of global drug sales, compared with the five percent shares held by the current leaders, Novartis and Britain's Glaxo Wellcome Plc.

And he added: "We want to be a leader in the fields we compete in, and we want to be at the forefront of innovation and to have a solid and forceful market presence, so it is important to be in the major league. But to be number one, two or three that really doesn't matter at all."

Vasella said Novartis, which recently strengthened its position in generics with the acquisition of Germany's Azupharma, and in biotech by completing the purchase of California's SyStemix, would constantly seek to augment its global network of 400 research alliances.

"You need to constantly scout what is going on (in science). If we see something emerging where we see a fit we will obviously try to partner. On the other hand we have all the technologies in house of genomics and combinatorial chemistry and it is important to also foster internal know-how."
Vasella said job-cutting as a result of the merger was "on target," with 4,600 already leaving the company. The target over three years is a reduction of "ten to twelve thousand."
